items.heading: SILVER JUBILEE RELAY
items.summary: Bill Laws's report on Blackheath Harriers' Silver Jubilee 25 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace on 19 June 1977, where non-appearances forced Belgrave runners to double up but youngsters ran promising times, with the full stage-by-stage times of the A, B, Vets. and Under 17 teams.
items.text:
JUNE 19th 1977 - CRYSTAL PALACE.

SILVER JUBILEE RELAY

Departing from the popular 100 x 1 mile format Blackheath Harriers celebrated Silver Jubilee year by reducing all teams to 25 stages of 1 mile each. The correspondingly large increase in the number of teams meant more runners on the track at any particular time and at Crystal Palace 24 teams took to the tartan in the morning and 20 of the faster teams in the afternoon.

Belgrave entered a Vets. and Under 17 team in the morning and an A & B team in the afternoon. Due to the non-appearance of 25 runners several people competed twice, sometimes in 2 teams, to enable final times to be gained. Perhaps the bigger disappointment was in the Vets. team where, due to the non-appearance of 3 vets. doubling up became necessary. The final time of 2 hrs.22min.22secs. easily beat the winning vets. time of 2 hrs.30min.9.6secs. set by Sale Harriers and with 3 more of our better vets. 2 hrs.20mins. would have been on the cards.

The running of two teams at a time put a strain on the handful of Belgrave officials who turned up to help out and it was almost inevitable that something would go wrong. Steve Williams was the unfortunate one - he hadn't stripped off ready to take stage 14 for the A team and his time represents some kind of record for running to the change-over point and doing a striptease while running the first 2 laps.

There were however some very encouraging performances. In the A team Jamie Stevenson ran a stalwart first leg and Robin Brown confirmed Gordon Biscoe's predictions by running an immaculate 10th stage. John Bicourt ran a relaxed 4.20 before being rushed to Victoria Coach Station by Tom Carter to join the England team travelling to Turin. The most promising signs came from the Boys, Colts and Youths all of whom thoroughly enjoyed their racing. Checking on last year's times shows that all of them substantially improved their previous bests and some times were very good indeed. John Searle ran 5:04 and 5:05, Alan Perriam 5:07 and 5:00 but pride of place must go to 13 year old Matthew Cannon who confirmed that some of his reported timings at school were not way-out by running 5:03. Miss Baker became the first young lady to run for Belgrave in the event and Miss Pritchard the second - albeit as a protesting reserve but enabling the U.17 team to finish. Incidentally it is worth noting that the U.17 team's average age was 14 and if the youngsters keep up progress Belgrave's hopes for the future are high.

Organisation of the teams proved once again how many of our active members fall out of circulation each year. This year, of the 110 runners entered, only 39 had run in 1976 and only 22 in 1975! Let's hope more people stay with it for next year.

Finally my thanks to those who once again helped to make it all possible; especially Bill Couzens and Keith Sinclair on time recording. Brian Pritchard and John Baker on booking in arrivals and Gordon Doubleday on stopwatch.

Bill Laws.

SILVER JUBILEE RELAY

143 complete teams finished.

items.text:
Do you know where the 'Olympic Games' were held between the years 1636 and 1850? Turn to page 53 for the answer.

THE 1636 OLYMPICS

After the death of the ancient Olympic Games in 393 AD there was a lapse in sporting activities but at the Renaissance, naturally, there was renewed interest. It was in the heart of the Cotswolds that Robert Dover held his Games in 1636, and they continued until 1850 when Dr. Penny Brooke founded the Much Wenlock Olympian Society.

items.heading: TRACK AND FIELD
items.summary: Track and field notes for summer 1977: Gerry Deegan's club 3,000m best and Irish 5,000m win, Glyn Ratcliffe's discus club record, Cliff Brooks's decathlon, Mark Shippen's pole vault and Ernie Obeng's sprint records.
items.text:
TRACK AND FIELD

Gerry Deegan became the fastest ever Belgravian over 3,000 metres at Crystal Palace on May 18th. In the Philips Silver Jubilee Night of Athletics, he placed 7th in 7:59.1. At Limerick on June 2nd he took Eire's colours past the post first in the 5,000 m. with 13:57.0 in the Ireland v Greece international.

John Bicourt gained selection for Britain in the GB v Italy v USA meeting at Turin on June 21st but was well down on his times of the past few years with 8:53.1 for 6th.

John Stow, in Surrey's side for the SCAAA v Surrey v Wales v Police match on May 29th was unplaced in the 1500m. but nevertheless clocked 3:56.0 - a promising early season time.

May 28/29th saw Cliff Brooks reaching his second best ever score in the inter-area decathlon at Southampton, adding 195 points to his A.A.A. Champs. 7th place tally earlier in the month. Among the ten events were two equal personal bests for Cliff - a 1.89m high jump and a 15.6 hurdles - and his final score of 6,695 was just 12 points shy of his own Barbados National and Belgrave record.

Glyn Ratcliffe was in fine form at Aldershot on 15/16th June where the Army Championships were being held. He took the discus title with 50.42m - a new Club record - and also managed 14.04m for 3rd in the shot. Other important wins have gone to Glyn in the Inter-Services Championship (47.72m) and Surrey v Hants v Army (48.88m).

Representing Surrey in this latter meeting Cliff Brooks placed 2nd over the 400m hurdles in 56.0 and Ernie Obeng again had the beating of Danny Laing but was in turn beaten by the Army's S.Hall - both recorded 10.8 for the 100m. Pride of place however, must go to our Super-youth Mark Shippen, clearing 4 metres yet again to take 3rd in this senior pole-vault competition.

Going back again to the Army Champs at Aldershot, second over 400m hurdles was Mel Ford who we have not seen for a few years but was a regular in our league teams a while back. His time of 55.6 was not too far down on the winner, Walcot Taylor, and just to underline his current fitness Mel raced to victory in the Midland Counties A.A.A. Champs a few days later with 54.6.

Ernie Obeng was our only finallist in the Southern Champs. with his 6th place in the 200m - 21.83. He was an unlucky non-qualifier in the short sprint with 10.76, as was Paul Whitby with his 15.69 high hurdles.

Just four days after his record breaking exploit at Haringey in our fourth league match, Ernie was back again at the same track, exploding to two more outstanding sprint times. He equalled his new Club 100m mark of 10.6 and also shaved a tenth off Steve White's 200m record with 21.5. He has not left things to rest there however, for in August in an Open Meeting at West London he cut that 100m time again - to 10.5.

items.heading: APRIL 30th/MAY 1st 1977 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY COUNTY A.A.A. CHAMPS. PART I.
items.summary: Report on the first part of the Surrey County AAA Championships at Motspur Park, 30 April-1 May 1977, where Peter Crosbie won the junior pentathlon with a club record 2,598 points.
items.text:
APRIL 30th/MAY 1st 1977 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY COUNTY A.A.A. CHAMPS. PART I.

Peter Crosbie added yet another county championship to his tally when he opened the 1977 season with a clear win in the junior pentathlon. In spite of actually winning only one of the five events, his speciality the javelin, his overall victory was by a convincing 100 points and his score of 2,598 constituted a new Club Record. Peter's individual performances were LJ 5.80, JT 53.66, 200 26.3, DT 30.78, 1500 4:59.0.

Our senior relay squad had been tipped for a possible win but in their first outing of the year together the change-overs were a bit "rusty" and they were beaten by a slick Croydon team, 43.2 to 42.7. Both were inside the old championship best.

Leo Coy placed 6th in the steeplechase with 10:30.2, Pete Gardner ran to a PB of 9:45.0 in the junior 3,000 metres and over the two days Reg. Hopkins piled up 5,581 points for 2nd in the decathlon.

items.heading: League starts with a win
items.summary: Report and results of Southern League match 1 at Wimbledon Park on 7 May 1977, won by Belgrave from Hercules Wimbledon thanks to Charlie Gillett's last leg in the 4 x 400 metres.
items.text:
MAY 7th 1977 - WIMBLEDON PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 1.

League starts with a win

Belgrave took the lead early in the afternoon but never had any chance of breaking away completely and as the relays came up Hercules Wimbledon were well within striking distance. In the final event, the 4 x 400 metres, they needed to beat us by three places to take the match and were doing just that before Charlie Gillett unleashed his full fury on the opposition on the last leg to save the day. Our winning points tally was enough to place the Club second overall in the league - a fine start.

New member Jim Preston made a sparkling debut in winning both his hurdle races and Reg. Hopkins confirmed that he was in good shape by being our highest points scorer of the match. A fighting Jamie Stevenson boosted our middle distance points, running a personal best 800 metres in his first 1977 track race and in fact each of the middle distance events gave us at least 6 points, an improvement on how things stood at the end of last season.

Stretching their unbeaten series of league sprints from one year to the next, Ernest Obeng and Jim Evans looked superb, with Ernie drawing gasps from the spectators each time he went into action. His first leg in the sprint relay seemed unbelievable as he rocketed past the opposing teams in the staggered lanes outside him, putting the Bels ahead after 100 metres with the advantage of the second bend still to come.

An event as exciting as any was the pole vault where young Mark Shippen came up against ex-international Jeff Fenge of H.W. It was great to see our man come out on top.

items.summary: Report and results of the second part of the Surrey AAA Championships at Motspur Park on 14 May 1977, where Ernest Obeng won the 100m in 10.9 and was second to Danny Laing in the 200m, and juniors Peter Crosbie (javelin) and Mark Shippen (pole vault) won titles.
items.text:
MAY 14th 1977 - MOTSPUR PARK - SURREY AAA CHAMPS. PART II.

Our double champion from last year's meeting, Jim Evans, has been finding things tough recently with injuries, moving home, etc. but Belgrave's colours were kept to the fore in the sprints thanks to Ernest Obeng, competing in his first "Surrey". He qualified for the 100m final with the fastest time and then sped to a 10.9 victory over South London's Danny Laing, 11.1. In the 200m Ernie impressively took his heat in 21.9, six metres clear of Croydon's ace sprinter Bob Benn, but come the final which was the last event in the nine hour programme, Danny Laing got his revenge with a 21.7 to Ernie's 22.3.

No other senior medals came our way although there were a good sprinkling of 4ths. Cliff Brooks was cock-a-hoop with his 40.34m discus throw, beating a ten year old pb. On a brief holiday in the old country, John Thresher was our sole representative in the 5000m and we had no-one out at all in the 1,500m.

Our junior athletes provided two winners in Peter Crosbie - his 6th successive javelin title - and youth Mark Shippen who collected the pole vault with no opposition.

items.summary: Report and results of Southern League match 2 at Bedford on 28 May 1977, where a makeshift Belgrave team without Cliff Brooks and Ernest Obeng finished fourth and fell to 9th overall.
items.text:
MAY 28th 1977 - BEDFORD - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 2.

Bedford Blues

Our win in match 1 had placed us in second spot in the league and ready for great things but match 2 was where it all started to go wrong. With Cliff Brooks down at Southampton busy putting together a fine decathlon and Ernest Obeng suffering a pulled thigh muscle, our league team was suddenly a very makeshift outfit. Hot competition came from the up and coming Bedford and Chelmsford teams and with our older rivals Cambridge H. and Windsor also present the Bels. had an uphill battle keeping out of last place.

Jim Preston suffering from "the night before" did not enjoy his 400m hurdles at all but by the time his high hurdles race came up he had recovered to give us one of our few wins. The other first places came from Reg Hopkins and Arnold Bentt in the jumps and Jamie Stevenson in the 800m. Reg also set his best ever time in the 200m.

Young David Bailey who seems to have been around for years but is still only a first year junior impressed all with his very relaxed 4 x 400 relay run, coming on strong at the end of his lap. Surely his place in the team will now be a standard booking. Les Davies made his debut in Belgrave colours with 2nd in the triple and long jumps and is a most welcome addition to our ranks, whilst David Bradford came close to his best in the 1500m.

So, fourth place it was in the end - sending us plummetting down to 9th overall.

items.heading: O'Hara again
items.summary: Report and result of the club 10,000 metres championship at Battersea Park on 8 June 1977, Laurie O'Hara's seventh consecutive win and eighth Tom Carter Cup, ahead of Colin Pearson and Lionel Mann.
items.text:
JUNE 8th 1977 - BATTERSEA PARK - CLUB 10,000M CHAMPIONSHIP.

O'Hara again

Ten days short of his 45th birthday the remarkable Laurie O'Hara gained his seventh consecutive win in the Club 10Km championship and has now taken home the 'Tom Carter' cup on eight occasions all told. As the years go by the margin of his superiority remains as great as ever and he appears to be in no danger of being caught by any of our current members. This time his win was by over a minute and the entire field, barring Colin Pearson, was lapped at least once. The only flaw in Laurie's astounding record is the fact that he has not as yet gained the championship best time, his fastest in this race being 30:57.6 in '72 compared to Bob Smith's 30:31.2 in 1969 when the race first went metric.

Overshadowed but not going unnoticed, Lionel Mann picked up his eighth place medal from the last ten races, having won in 1970. A second class standard medal went to Brian Gorman as a reward for turning in his fastest time for some years and Jamie Stevenson impressed onlookers by keeping well up the field throughout; no need for surprise, however, for Jamie seems to be a natural at any distance that he cares to tackle from 400 metres upwards.

items.heading: Bouncing Bentt
items.summary: Report and results of Southern League match 3 at Croydon on 25 June 1977, where Belgrave were second to Blackheath, with Arnold Bentt's 13.99m triple jump and two junior records for Matthew King.
items.text:
JUNE 25th 1977 - CROYDON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 3.

Bouncing Bentt

Finishing as second team kept us from slipping further down the league. We might have hoped to beat Blackheath H. before the event but their new member, international Mike Winch, not surprisingly made them a gift of the discus, shot and hammer and of course this also made their previous 'A' thrower a mighty powerful 'B' man; the 'Heathens' were therefore unstoppable on this occasion.

Star of the Belgrave team for the afternoon was Arnold Bentt who suddenly and for no apparent reason added a "Beamon-like" improvement to his previous best triple jump. In 1973 Arnie was pleased to record a 13.30m effort but had not improved since, so this day's leap of 13.99m left him and others of our team astounded.

On the cinders a track-suited Ernest Obeng guarding his injured leg against the cold still kept ahead of all others in the sprints. Paul Whitby and James Preston gave us maximum points in the high hurdles while Cliff Brooks broke new ground with a 52 metre javelin throw and succeeded in making Peter Crosbie a winning 'B' man for the day.

Young Matthew King made a welcome first appearance for us and in picking up 1st in the 'B' discus and 2nd in the 'B' shot established two new junior records. It appears that our overall strength in jumps and throws is now leaving our middle distance men behind in points gathering and will soon be challenging our sprinters and hurdlers.

items.heading: Four records smashed
items.summary: Report and results of Southern League match 4 at Haringey on 2 July 1977, where Belgrave were second to Haringey & Southgate, with Ernest Obeng's 10.6 100m, a 42.3 club 4x100 relay record and Mark Shippen's 4.15m pole vault (the heading says four records, the text three).
items.text:
JULY 2nd 1977 - HARINGEY - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 4.

Four records smashed

So often we seem to rise to the occasion when the opposition is at its greatest. A win against the very strong Haringey & Southgate club was never on the cards but our boys did us proud with fine performances all round and three new Club records.

Our sprinters were superb. Ernest Obeng swept away our complicated 100 metres list with a devastating 10.6 seconds and then started our 4 x 100 metres relay squad off to another Belgrave best - 42.3 secs - thus erasing that 1954 A.A.A. winning time from the record books.

With our sprinters faster than any who have competed in claret and gold before, Mark Shippen now set about making himself highest ever Belgravian by tackling 4.21 metres in the pole vault. He had already smashed by 15 centimetres his own junior and youth marks of 4.00 metres to win the event but now some doubt existed as to the height of our senior record. Was it 4.19m.....4.20m perhaps? No one seemed to know for sure so Mark had the bar set at 4.21m. He wasn't too far away and it will not be long before he does beat that senior best of 4.18 metres.

Nice running came from another of our youngsters Dave Bailey. His 400 metres showed just a hint of what this boy could be capable of with regular training.

items.text:
JULY 30th 1977 - CROYDON - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 5.

A day to forget

This was the day when everything went wrong for the Bels. Dropped relay batons, runners pulling out in mid race, members turning up to support and finding themselves toeing the starting line - it all happened for our penultimate match. Luckily the clubs placed behind us in the league table were some points down so even with only two match points gained after a couple of hours of trials and tribulations our overall league position remained unchanged - 8th.

The appearance of Glyn Ratcliffe's huge frame gave the Bels something to enthuse over but surprisingly even he, the Army Champion, was beaten in the discus. It just goes to show the standard of competition these days.

At long last Ernest Obeng's unbeaten run came to an end. He took the 100 metres for his 19th consecutive league win but his young North London opponent had pressed him hard and in the longer sprint the decision was reversed.

items.heading: Bels finish with a flourish
items.summary: Report and results of Southern League match 6 at Battersea Park on 20 August 1977, won by Belgrave on newly equipped grounds, lifting the club over Blackheath to a final 7th in Division 1.
items.text:
AUGUST 20th 1977 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN LEAGUE MATCH 6.

Bels finish with a flourish

"We start as we mean to go on and we finish as well as we start but something always seems to go wrong in the middle of the season." Our Field Events Secretary has never said truer words than these, spoken after our exciting win in the final match.

Battersea Park, not previously known for its fine athletic facilities had never looked better. Brand new equipment was on show everywhere: pole vault stands and landing beds, a hammer/discus cage, new high jump stands, all-weather javelin run-up, a cleaned up shot putt area and even a proper "laps-to-go" sign, all were there for our use thanks to the G.L.C. Parks Dept. (and the regular harrassment of the Parks Dept. by our Committee).

The javelin run-up gave Peter Crosbie a boost as he launched his second longest throw ever and another to take full advantage of the new equipment was Mark Shippen. After winning at 4 metres Mark had the bar set at 4.20m in another attempt to make the Belgrave Senior Club Record his own. He cleared on his third try....only to dislodge the bar with his arm on the way down.

The trackmen, of course, were still competing on the sluggish Battersea cinders but Ernest Obeng does not seem to worry what surface he runs on. He zipped to 10.9 in the 100 metres and with a winning lead of four tenths one could easily understand how he clocked 10.5 during the week on an all-weather track. Jim Evans backed up as reliably as ever in the 'B' sprints.

John Bicourt turned out to give us a 5000m/1500m double and Ian Duncan, fitting into our team very nicely, scored well in the 'B' 1500, but again the most exciting race was the 4 x 400 metres relay. With our team looking for a fourth member, Ernest Obeng was cajoled into running his first ever 400. Jamie Stevenson, suffering from a cold, handed over near the front but soon Ernie was loping along in the rear, coolly taking his pace from the other runners. When they hit the straight he exploded into action and gave Reg Hopkins a slight lead. While Ernie recovered from "rubbery legs" the race see-sawed back and forth until Charlie Gillett again took the claret and gold to the front of the tightly bunched group with only 50 metres left. Ilford's man pipped him on the line to finally win the race, as thrilling as any international.

This team victory leap-frogged us over Blackheath H in the league chart for a final 7th place among the 25 clubs in Division 1.

items.text:
SEPTEMBER 3rd 1977 - WEST LONDON STADIUM - LONDON A.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS

In the GLC Championships our ace sprinters were again to the fore. Ernie Obeng was a clear winner of the 100 metres in 10.6, two tenths clear of a "blanket-finish" for second place. International Les Hoyte (Thames Valley) was awarded the silver medal with our Jim Evans in 5th place but sharing the same time, 10.8, as Hoyte. It was an equal personal best for Jim.

Ernie handed another defeat to Hoyte in the 200m although this time they were both given the same time of 21.7, whilst 5th place again went to Jim with 22.6.

Jamie Stevenson placed 6th over 800m in 1:58.8 and Belgrave finished up third for the Club Trophy with 12 points to Thames Valley's 32 and Shaftesbury's 23.

Graham has had a remarkable year, clocking up a couple of fast mile races against Ilford's Roger Mills at the Crystal Palace, winning the Club 3,000 metre championship in 12:31.8 and following this time with a lightning 12:14.9 for 2nd in the A.A.A. Victor in the G.L.C. Championships in 12:33.2, breaking Paul Nihill's record by seven seconds, he has also led the field to the finish in the Enfield 20km (91:01), the Ilford 10km (43:09) and the Lambeth 10km (44:43). 1977 has seen Graham emerge as one of the main contenders for the Commonwealth Games in Edmonton, Canada next year.
